q: Germinating peas used 0.12, 0.25 and 0.49 mL O2 per gram per hour at 10, 20 and 30°C, but only 0.08 at 45°C. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Rate increases in a straight line with temperature across the whole range that was tested
Rate falls at 45°C because oxygen becomes much more soluble in water at higher temperatures
Temperature has no real effect on respiration rate, because peas are not able to regulate it
Rate about doubles per 10°C to 30°C as collisions increase, then falls as enzymes denature
explanation: 0.12 → 0.25 → 0.49 roughly doubles per 10°C (Q10 ≈ 2), typical of enzyme-catalysed reactions: more kinetic energy means more frequent enzyme–substrate collisions. The sharp drop at 45°C suggests respiratory enzymes have denatured (active sites changed shape). O2 actually becomes less soluble as temperature rises, and an organism that can't regulate its temperature is more affected, not less.
